messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple CUDA OOMs observed on pool us-west-2-gpu-3 within the last 3m. Autoscaler reported node flaps and runtime reported 'cudaMalloc failed' errors despite headroom metrics showing ~1.1GB free. Initiating incident thread.
ryan_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Seeing a spike in 503s from generation route 'text-gen-large'. Routing already degraded to fallback.
anna_sre: pinging in — quick note: we've seen similar before where reserved block accounting + fragmentation left unusable free memory. Need allocator state and nvml snapshots.
maya_ml-runtime: logs from runtimes:
```\n[2026-10-12T10:24:11Z] ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 134217728 bytes)
[2026-10-12T10:24:11Z] INFO mem: reported headroom 1.12GB, reserved_blocks 256MB, slab_free 128MB
[2026-10-12T10:24:12Z] WARN kvcache: attempted eviction but active sessions prevented reclaim
```
ryan_oncall: interesting — headroom shows free but allocation still fails. Could be fragmentation or reserved blocks pinned by older sessions.
liu_infra: I'm running nvml and allocator dump now: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-dump --node us-west-2-gpu-3 --out /tmp/dump.tgz` — ETA ~90s.
jess_support: Customers A and B reported intermittent 503s, ticket #INC-4629 and #INC-4632. Both on hosted tier, affected between 10:23-10:30 UTC. Noting impact in status page now.
anna_sre: mitigation idea 1: drain affected node from scheduler (no new tasks), trigger runtime to evict KV caches aggressively, then restart runtime process to reclaim reserved slabs. Mitigation idea 2: temporarily reduce reserve configuration from 256MB -> 64MB for this pool to avoid headroom mismatch (safe temporary).
maya_ml-runtime: to add: for large models we pre-allocate caches and kv segments; if sessions keep shards pinned, you can see free linear memory but fragmentation prevents large contiguous allocation. We had a hotfix before that reduced per-session kv prefetch.
ryan_oncall: doing node drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-37 && kubectl drain gpu-node-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting eviction of pods.
anna_sre: while drain happens, please run `runtimectl snapshot-allocator --node gpu-node-37` and attach the output here. That shows reserved vs free extents.
liu_infra: dump attached to thread: /mnt/logs/allocator-snapshot-gpu-node-37.txt (uploaded). Quick snippet: 
```\nAllocator summary:
  Total GPU mem: 40GB
  Used by processes: 32.3GB
  Reserved blocks (kernel): 256MB
  Fragmented free: 800MB across 48 extents
  Largest free extent: 72MB
```
maya_ml-runtime: that explains it — largest free extent 72MB, but requests ask for 128MB+ contiguous chunks leading to cudaMalloc OOM despite ~800MB total free.
ryan_oncall: thanks. So plan: 1) keep node drained, 2) evict and restart runtime on node to defragment, 3) update autoscaler to avoid scheduling heavy generation on remaining nodes while we recover, 4) temporarily route heavy requests to smaller model variant.
jess_support: posting incident notice to customers with ETA ~30m for full recovery; informing customers of degraded throughput fallback to smaller model.
oliver_product: also flagging highest-usage customers for manual outreach. Anything we can do to avoid recurrence next week?
anna_sre: followups: long-term: introduce periodic slab compaction on idle, adjust reserved_block config to be size-class aware, and add a headroom health check that looks at largest_free_extent not just sum free. Short-term: lower reserved blocks to 64MB for the pool and enable aggressive kvcache eviction policy.
liu_infra: restarted runtime process on gpu-node-37 — pods coming back up, running liveness checks. Perf monitor shows no immediate OOMs as runtime warms.
maya_ml-runtime: validating with probe traffic: sending a few synthetic 1k token generation requests. If these succeed we can uncordon.
ryan_oncall: probe succeeded for 10/10 requests. Uncordoning now: `kubectl uncordon gpu-node-37`.
anna_sre: monitoring for 15m. If we see repeat, we'll roll a config change cluster-wide.
ryan_oncall: handoff to next oncall @liu_infra for follow-up and postmortem collection — checklist: attach allocator dump, nvml snapshots, runtime logs, list affected request IDs, and the tickets.
liu_infra: acked, will own postmortem. I'll collect /mnt/logs/* and create an RCA doc.
jess_support: updated customers and cleared immediate SLA impact for now (will follow up with root cause).
oliver_product: please include recommended mitigation in postmortem (model routing heuristics + size-class headroom check).
anna_sre: quick todo captured:
- Add largest_free_extent metric to node health exporter
- Add periodic runtime compaction job for idle GPUs
- Review default reserved_block size for large-model nodes
- Add integration test that allocates large contiguous pages to catch fragmentation regressions
ryan_oncall: thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated for now. Leaving channel open for postmortem thread and notes. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (10:47 UTC). Follow-up owner: liu_infra. Postmortem due in 72h. :memo:
liu_infra: I'll create the postmortem draft and tag owners. Expect first pass in ~24h.
maya_ml-runtime: adding test case to repo to reproduce fragmentation locally (script + small allocator sim). Will link PR in postmortem.
anna_sre: one more thing — add a canary that simulates a bunch of long-lived small allocations to test fragmentation over time.
ryan_oncall: handing off. Next oncall please watch the 'generation-heavy' route for 2h.
liu_infra: taking it.
